nodes.label: compose: relay service (target runtime)
nodes.rationale: target: runtime is explicit and load-bearing -- with no target Docker builds the LAST stage (capture), so the web app silently shipped Chromium and ran as the capture user.

nodes.label: compose: worker service (init, health, cache-hit args)
nodes.rationale: Runs the pipeline out of band so a download never occupies a request handler; init:true because Bun as PID 1 does not reap yt-dlp/ffmpeg/instaloader grandchildren; the NEXT_PUBLIC args are repeated to keep the build a cache hit; depends_on relay is a migration ordering constraint, not a runtime one.

nodes.label: compose: capture service (Chromium, shm, seccomp)
nodes.rationale: Its own service because Next.js cannot upgrade a WebSocket and the cap needs one owner process; shm_size 1gb because Docker's 64MB /dev/shm crashes tabs; seccomp:unconfined with cap_drop ALL so Chromium can apply its own tighter per-renderer filter instead of running --no-sandbox; only /stream should ever be routed publicly; relay_data is deliberately not mounted.

nodes.label: compose: dragonfly service (pinned, allow-undeclared-keys)
nodes.rationale: --default_lua_flags=allow-undeclared-keys is required because BullMQ's Lua builds key names at runtime; pinned rather than :latest because Coolify pulls on every deploy, so a floating tag can change the queue backend under an app-only deploy.

nodes.label: CAPTURE_INTERNAL_TOKEN (dedicated inter-service secret)
nodes.rationale: A dedicated secret with a `:?` guard so compose refuses to start without it; the config's VAULT_KEY fallback exists only for a zero-config dev box, and shipping it would send the master encryption key as an HTTP header between containers.

nodes.label: compose: json-file log rotation on every service
nodes.rationale: Container logs are unbounded by default and the deploy target is a single VPS, while Coolify's cleanup prunes images rather than log files.
